newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up on finance company buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up on finance company buying.

text.p: Thai stocks closed up on Thursday, amid buying of finance counters, and on talk the prime minister may change his finance minister if he survived an ongoing censure debate against him, brokers said.
The SET Index rose nearly 1.0 percent or 9.83 points to 1047.86 in thin dealings.

Brokers said afternoon gains were spurred by speculation that a special economic advisor to the government Siam Commercial Bank president Olarn Chaipravat might replace current Finance Minister Bodi Chunannanda. Some foreign buying of finance companies also helped as local joined in.

Wall Street Finance and Securities analyst Youssef Aboud said: "The rumours (on the finance minister) began in mid-afternoon. They boosted sentiment since they were seen psychologically compensating the business community should Banharn stay on after the censure debate."

Volumes was 4.208 billion baht. Advancers topped decliners 231 to 82 while 96 issues closed unchanged. The SET 50 rose 0.75 points to 80.35 points. Finance stocks were among top preformers, Capital Nomura Securities (CNS.BK) gained 3.25 baht to 36.25 baht while CMIC Finance and Securities (CMIC.BK) gained 4.75 baht to 53.50.
National Finance and Securities (NFS.BK) was the top traded stock and gained 2.50 baht to 72.50 baht.
A First Asia Securities analyst Virat Tippananontakul said the market was expected to move sideways on Friday with support seen at 1020 and resistance at 1060.
Politics wpuld again hang over trading patterns as the censure debate moved into its third day tomorrow. --James Mclean-- (662) 6520642
